body.title: fix: preserve flag parsing when an argument matches a command
body.body:
## What type of PR is this?

- bug

## What this PR does / why we need it:

With a root `--verbose` flag and a `deploy` child, `app file deploy --verbose` runs the root action with `verbose=false` and arguments `["file", "deploy", "--verbose"]`. Replacing `deploy` with an ordinary word correctly sets the flag. A command alias has the same effect. A padded first argument, `" deploy "`, also stops parsing even though dispatch preserves it as an argument.

`parseFlags` hands off the remaining arguments whenever a trimmed positional token matches a child, but dispatch only selects a child from the exact first positional argument. If a later argument happens to be a command name, parsing stops and no child takes over.

Only hand parsing to a child when the exact first positional argument selects it. The root then parses its remaining flags normally, while first-position command names and aliases still dispatch as before.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

No existing issue found. Found with a standalone program using the public API; searches for positional arguments, command names, and `parseFlags` found no competing fix for this case.

## Special notes for your reviewer:

#2541 changes the same parser block to handle shorthand command names. I checked this guard together with that change and the other pending command fixes; the combined race suite passes. I will reconcile the small overlap if either parser change lands first.

## Testing

On macOS arm64 with Go 1.26.5, based on upstream `d5c06cb`:

- `TestCommand_ChildNameAfterPositionalArgument` fails for a later command name, a later alias, and a command name following an empty argument. The ordinary-argument and first-position dispatch controls pass. Those six cases pass with the initial fix; stashing only that production change reproduces the three failures. A seventh case for a padded first argument fails on the initial PR head `91df506`, then passes when lookup uses the exact argument; stashing that follow-up reproduces its failure.
- The standalone program changes from `verbose=false args=["file" "deploy" "--verbose"]` to `verbose=true args=["file" "deploy"]`.
- `make ensure-goimports lint vet test`
- `make test GFLAGS='--tags urfave_cli_no_template'`
- `make check-binary-size generate v3diff diffcheck`
- `golangci-lint run`: 0 issues.

The test targets include the race detector. Linux/Windows and the other CI Go version were not run locally.

## Release Notes

```release-note
Command names used as later positional arguments, and padded arguments that resemble command names, no longer prevent later flags from being parsed by the current command.
```

body.title: fix: run flag actions for values set in Before
body.body:
## What type of PR is this?

- bug

## What this PR does / why we need it:

Calling `cmd.Set("region", "west")` in `Before` updates the flag value and makes `IsSet("region")` true, but its flag action never runs unless the flag was already set by argv or an environment source. The same hook therefore triggers the action for `app --region east` but skips it for `app`.

`Command.Set` updates the flag without adding it to the command's `setFlags` map. Record successful sets there so the existing flag-action phase sees them. Failed sets return their existing error, and setting a flag before command setup still works with an initially nil map.

The regression covers an unset root flag, argv and environment controls, and an inherited flag set through its alias in a child command's `Before` hook.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

No existing issue found. Related completed work: #2221 made environment-sourced flags participate in the same action phase.

## Special notes for your reviewer:

This keeps the existing lifecycle order. It does not invoke actions immediately inside `Set` or run actions for untouched defaults. Persistent flag actions retain their existing per-command behavior: if the flag is set in both a parent and a child, its action runs in both contexts. A parent argv value followed by a child `Before` call to `Set` now behaves like setting the flag via argv in both contexts.

## Testing

On macOS arm64 with Go 1.26.5:

- The regression fails on upstream `d5c06cb` for unset and inherited flags; argv and environment controls pass. All four pass with the fix. Stashing only the production change reproduces the two failures.
- A standalone public-API program prints only `command action: west (set=true)` on upstream. With the fix it first prints `flag action: west`.
- `make ensure-goimports lint vet test`
- `make test GFLAGS='--tags urfave_cli_no_template'`
- `make check-binary-size generate v3diff diffcheck`
- `golangci-lint run`: 0 issues.

Both local test targets include the race detector. Native Linux/Windows and the other CI Go version have not been run locally.

## Release Notes

```release-note
Flags set with Command.Set in a Before hook now participate in flag actions even when no command-line argument or environment source previously set them.
```

body.title: fix: parse child flags after shorthand command names
body.body:
## What type of PR is this?

- bug

## What this PR does / why we need it:

With `PrefixMatchCommands: true`, `app depl --region west` rejects a flag declared on `deploy`, even though `app deploy --region west` works. If the root also declares `--region`, the abbreviated invocation succeeds but sets the root flag instead; the child action receives its default value.

`parseFlags` only recognizes exact command names and explicit aliases. It parses the remaining flags on the parent before `run` resolves the shorthand through `SuggestCommandFunc`.

Resolve the first positional argument while locating the child command, then let that child parse the remaining flags. Parsing and dispatch share the result, so a custom matcher is called once per invocation. An unmatched name still leaves subsequent flags for the parent, and the cached match is local to each run.

The regression tests cover full names, aliases, shorthand with long and short flags, a custom matcher with a shadowed parent flag, an unmatched name, repeated runs, and preserving the existing shell-completion path.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

No existing issue found. Searches for `PrefixMatchCommands`, `SuggestCommandFunc`, and shorthand command flags found no competing fix.

## Special notes for your reviewer:

A custom matcher now runs when parsing reaches the first positional argument, before flags following it are parsed. This is necessary to choose which command owns those flags.

#2534 addresses command names following `--`; this change addresses flags following a shorthand command name. Both touch dispatch, so I will reconcile them if either merges first.

## Testing

On macOS arm64 with Go 1.26.5:

- The new regression tests fail on upstream `d5c06cb`, pass with the fix, and fail again with only the production fix stashed.
- A standalone program with root and child `--region` flags prints `child region=child-default; root region=west` before the fix and `child region=west; root region=root-default` afterward.
- `make ensure-goimports lint vet test`
- `make test GFLAGS='--tags urfave_cli_no_template'`
- `make check-binary-size generate v3diff diffcheck`
- `golangci-lint run`: 0 issues.
- `make gfmrun FLAGS='--walk docs/v3/examples'`: 42 examples, 0 errors.

The local tests use the race detector. Linux, Windows, and the other Go version in the CI matrix have not been run locally.

## Release Notes

```release-note
Flags following a shorthand command name are now parsed by the selected child command, instead of being rejected or applied to a same-named parent flag.
```

body.title: fix: reject overridden flag aliases in descendant commands
body.body:
## What type of PR is this?

- bug

## What this PR does / why we need it:

A persistent flag overridden by an intermediate command becomes available again under its old alias in deeper subcommands. With a root `--config/-c` and a `deploy` command defining its own `--config`:

```text
app deploy -c prod                 # rejects -c
app deploy service -c prod         # runs, but service reads config=""
app deploy service --config prod   # runs with config="prod"
```

The second command silently sets the root flag to `prod`, while `cmd.String("config")` reads the nearer override. That makes the same alias change behavior depending on the subcommand depth.

`parseFlags` gathers persistent flags from the nearest ancestor outward, but checks collisions only against flags declared on the current command. The check now includes flags already applied from nearer ancestors, so an overridden root flag stays excluded. The old alias is rejected consistently and the overriding flag still works.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

None filed; found while exercising nested command flag inheritance. Related completed work: #2421 and #2481.

## Testing

On macOS arm64, Go 1.26.5, from upstream `d5c06cb04479eeacbbb9378ea26261b6be516320`:

- `TestPersistentFlagOverrideInDescendants` fails on upstream for the old alias on child/grandchild commands and passes with this change. Stashing only the production change makes those cases fail again. The existing rejection on `deploy` and the surviving `--config` are also covered.
- A standalone program using the public API reproduces the three commands above; with the fix both `-c` invocations fail before the action runs.
- `make ensure-goimports`, `make lint`, `make vet`, `make test`, `make test GFLAGS='--tags urfave_cli_no_template'`, `make check-binary-size`, `make generate`, `make v3diff`, and `make diffcheck` pass. Both test targets include `-race`.
- `golangci-lint run` (2.15.0): 0 issues.

The Linux/Windows CI matrix and Go stable matrix were not run locally. No exported API changed.

## Release Notes

```release-note
An overridden persistent flag's alias no longer becomes available again in deeper subcommands and changes a different flag from the one the command reads.
```

body.title: fix: treat a command name after "--" as an argument
body.body:
## What type of PR is this?

- bug

## What this PR does / why we need it:

A `--` ends flag parsing, and everything after it should be an argument of the command. That works for flags, but the first argument after `--` is still looked up as a subcommand name:

```go
cmd := &cli.Command{
	Name:     "app",
	Action:   func(_ context.Context, c *cli.Command) error { fmt.Println("args:", c.Args().Slice()); return nil },
	Commands: []*cli.Command{{Name: "sub", Action: func(context.Context, *cli.Command) error { fmt.Println("sub ran"); return nil }}},
}
```

On `main`, `app -- sub` prints `sub ran`, and `app -- sub --x` fails with `flag provided but not defined: -x`, because `sub` then parses `--x` as a flag. Expected: the root action runs with `args: [sub]` and `args: [sub --x]`. Shell completion already follows this rule: since #2412 it suggests nothing after a `--`, "only positional arguments are accepted after it", so `app -- su<TAB>` offers nothing but `app -- sub` runs the subcommand.

- `command_parse.go`: `parseFlags` records when the parsed args start right after a `--` (nothing positional came before it).
- `command_run.go`: in that case the first arg is not looked up as a subcommand (or passed to `SuggestCommandFunc`). `DefaultCommand` still applies, so `app -- foo` behaves like `app foo` did before.
- `command.go`: the unexported field that holds this state.
- `command_test.go`: `TestCommand_CommandNameAfterTerminatorIsAnArgument`.

A `--` that comes after a positional argument (`app foo -- sub`) already worked, since `foo` was taken as the first argument.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

None, found while checking `--` handling with subcommands.

## Testing

- `TestCommand_CommandNameAfterTerminatorIsAnArgument` fails on `main` with `flag provided but not defined: -notAFlag` and `the subcommand must not run when its name follows "--"`, and passes with this change.
- `make vet`, `make test`, `make test GFLAGS='--tags urfave_cli_no_template'`, `make lint`, `make check-binary-size`, `make generate`, `make diffcheck` and `make v3diff` pass, and `golangci-lint run` reports 0 issues.

## Release Notes

```release-note
A command name given after "--" is now passed to the command as an argument instead of running that subcommand.
```
